title: Hitch a trailer: push its CURT ball coupler fully onto the 2 in ball, then latch it, not the other way round
instruction: Hitch the trailer to the ball.
context: Hitching a trailer to a car's tow ball is something most drivers who have rented a U-Haul trailer, towed a boat or a camper, or helped someone else do it, have watched or done. CURT's hook-up guide (curtmfg.com/hooking-trailer): latch up, lower the coupler onto the ball, and "with the coupler fully seated on the ball, engage the latch"; then jack the tongue up to test: "If it comes off the ball, it means that the coupler was not properly seated before being latched." Here the coupler hovers 25 mm over the ball with its handle up. The robot has to push the coupler straight down until the ball seats in the socket, then push the handle down until it latches, driving the underjaw under the ball. Pushed the other way round, the underjaw meets the ball and the handle jams part-way.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the bench top (the station table). A 2 in (50.8 mm) chrome hitch ball on a 19 mm shank stands on a dark 14 x 12 cm ball-mount base at (36, 22), on the left arm's side; the ball's centre is 7 cm above the bench. The trailer coupler (modelled on CURT 25153: 27 cm long, 5.2 cm wide; zinc socket head with a 52.4 mm pocket and a flared skirt; blue 2 in channel running back along +x) pivots on a fixed stand at x 58, so its socket can only swing up and down over the ball. At the start the coupler is tipped up 6.5 degrees, its socket 25 mm above the ball, centred over it; its yellow Posi-Lock handle (5.5 cm) is up at 60 degrees on top of the socket, and the red underjaw is retracted.
scoring: Seated: the coupler down within 0.5 degrees and its socket within 1.5 mm of the ball's centre. Latched: the handle within 3 degrees of closed and the underjaw fully in under the ball (within 2 mm of its full 65 mm stroke). At the end: 1.0 once seated and latched, everything at rest and no gripper point within 3 cm of the coupler, for 1 s; 0 whenever the coupler is latched with the ball not seated; 0.5 seated but not latched, at rest for 1 s; 0.25 lowered onto the ball (within 3 degrees) but not seated; 0 otherwise. The score is recomputed from the current state. Real trials: seated is checked as CURT says, by jacking the tongue up (it comes off the ball if it was not seated), and the underjaw from the side camera.
reset_notes: Lift the coupler back to its stop 25 mm above the ball and raise the handle; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Ball, socket ring and skirt are rigid colliders at real size (2 in ball, 0.4 mm radial clearance); the coupler is one hinged link on a fixed pivot, light (0.35 kg) so the arm can push it, not a 200 kg tongue. The handle is a hinge; the Posi-Lock linkage that drives the underjaw from the handle is a position drive in code (jaw follows the handle, saturating at 2 degrees), but the jaw is a real slider whose tines physically hit the ball if the coupler is not seated.
scores: Scripted (yam_arena sim, 320x176, seed 1): demo 1.0 (step 377); naive (handle first, jams; then coupler) 0.5; plate (coupler only) 0.5; same on Brev L40S. Dream-1 flash (seed 1): 0.0 in 700 steps, not refused.
